title: sqldex project configuration
description: The file that declares a schema project. Its presence is enough to declare one: every key below is optional, and an empty object is a complete file. The keys are snake_case because this is a format people write by hand.

sources.description: What builds the catalog. Omit to autodetect from the repository layout, which is what almost every project should do.

targets.description: What gets linted, when that is not the same as what builds the catalog. A deploy folder contributes no definitions — its CREATE TABLEs are copies — but it is code that runs and has to be checked. Omit for sources plus deploy_folder/**/*.sql where that directory exists.

schemas.description: Schemas whose tables live in this repository. Omit for the root directory's name. It exists so a reference into another database — other.orders when this repo is shop — is not checked against a same-named table of this one.

exclude.description: Names or globs to skip, relative to the root. Defaults to deploy.sql and rollback.sql, which are half a duplicated schema and would fill the catalog with phantom definitions.

diagnostics.description: What is reported, and how loudly. One mechanism at two widths: a whole group, or a single rule by id, which wins over its group.

enabled.description: Publish diagnostics while editing. Turning it off silences the editor and nothing else — `sqldex check` reports either way, so what CI fails on does not move with it. It is the blunt instrument; `groups` and `rules` are where a repo that dislikes two rules should go first.

groups.description: By group. { "audit": "off" } in a repository with no aud_ mirror-table convention.

names.description: The catalog contradicts the code: a name is not there, or it is ambiguous.

schema.description: The shape of the DDL: indexes, foreign keys, column types, primary keys.

query.description: What a statement does: joins, filters, NULL propagation, collations.

routine.description: The procedural side: arguments, variables, cursors.

audit.description: The aud_X mirror-table convention, which a repository either uses or does not.

rules.description: By rule id, group/name — the id the diagnostic carries, `sqldex rules` lists and `sqldex explain` takes. Ids are not enumerated here on purpose: a list in this file would be one more copy to keep in step with the engine, and a stale one would underline a rule that exists.

inlay_hints.description: The annotations drawn into the line rather than reported about it.

alias_tables.description: o gains shipments, the first time it appears in a statement.

call_parameters.description: A CALL's arguments gain the parameters they fill, OUT and INOUT named as such.

syntax_check.description: Whether a real MySQL grammar also checks the file, for a class of defect the fast backend's own permissive parser never detects on its own: a CREATE TABLE missing a comma, a mismatched BEGIN/END, a file that is not SQL at all. Inert if @sqldex/syntax-antlr is not installed.

enabled.description: On by default: silently skipping a correctness check most people would not think to go looking for a flag to enable is the wrong default.

dialect.description: Which engine the SQL is written for.

glob.description: Glob relative to the project root.

kind.description: A parsing hint, not a filter: it changes how much work is done, never what is found.
